description: loop() and while() statements, their iteration cap, and the condition rule that differs from every other boolean context.

cases.name: loop(n, body) runs the body n times
a loop count truncates toward zero
a negative loop count runs the body zero times
a loop body may hold several statements separated by semicolons
while(cond, body) repeats until the condition is zero
a while() condition tests EXACT zero, not the close-factor threshold
cases.note: PROVISIONAL, and the sharpest open question in this spec. Every other boolean context in EEL (if, &&, ||, !, bnot) treats |v| <= 1e-5 as false; while() does not, so a condition decaying to 1e-6 keeps looping here but would exit under the close-factor rule. Both CPU tiers agree, so the tier-differential fuzzers cannot see it. Confirm against ns-eel. If the close-factor rule is correct, x would be 0 and a class of presets currently spins to the iteration cap every frame.
